evidence.section: 3.2 High-temperature mechanical properties and fracture surface after annealing
evidence.quote: It can be inferred that at temperatures of 500 and 550 ◦ C, the deformation process is predominantly governed by work hardening, with the increase in flow stress attributed to a rise in dislocation density.

evidence.section: 3.2 High-temperature mechanical properties and fracture surface after annealing
evidence.quote: This deformation behavior indicates that dynamic recovery (DRV) and dynamic recrystallization (DRX) replace work hardening as the predominant factor in determining the deformation behavior.

evidence.section: 3.2 High-temperature mechanical properties and fracture surface after annealing
evidence.quote: A reasonable explanation is that DRX becomes more dominant above 650 ◦ C, exerting a substantial influence on the activation energy.

evidence.section: 3.2 High-temperature mechanical properties and fracture surface after annealing
evidence.quote: Given that DRV is believed to occur via dislocation glide, climb, or cross-slip, the required activation energy is close to the value of the self-diffusion activation energy.
